selenium: Replace not.toExist with isExisting to make things faster

tdf#94801 DOCX import: fix rounding error of table width

calculated by sum of table grid widths, converting twip
to 1/100 mm only at the end, with rounding up the width
instead of rounding down.
new_message_clean:
tdf#94801 DOCX import: fix table width loss by rounding

down the converted sum of table grid values. Small table
width loss (< 1/100 mm) could result big layout differences,
based on different line breaking etc.

When table width is calculated by sum of table grid widths,
now there is only a single conversion to 1/100 mm at the end,
with rounding up the width instead of rounding down.

Both grid and cell width values are stored in the
original twip instead of converting them to 1/100 mm
one by one, preventing regressions.

new_message_clean:
tdf#86790: Add support for a word-style styleref

STYLEREF is a field type in Word which changes its content based on
nearby paragraphs. For example, upon creating a styleref referencing
"Heading 1" you will see the text of the nearest "Heading 1"-styled
paragraph that is above the field.

This patch implements STYLEREF in Writer as a cross-reference. By using
"insert>cross-reference>styles" you'll be presented with a list of
styles. Selecting one and clicking "insert" will create a field which
has text from the "most relevant" instance of the style. To find the
most relevant instance we first search up for paragraphs with the style,
and if there are any we take the closest. If there weren't any, we
search down for paragraphs with the style.

This patch also updates our use of STYLEREF for chapters exported to
docx by using it for all chapters not only those in headers and footers.
This allows us to approximate more chapter field functionality even when
moving between Writer and Word.

old_message_clean:
Allow to opt in for --enable-gtk3 plus --without-system-cairo

This check had been introduced with 5ad60c5d69042a73d7a1632d3c04e15783817db4
"more configure, and scp2 pieces for gtk3 integration", but without stating any
reason. But at least my Linux build appears to work fine with (among others)

--enable-gtk3
--enable-gtk3-kde5
--without-system-cairo

And that combination proved useful to me when I wanted to run
SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN=gtk3 LO against a libcairo built with ASan the other day.

But to be on the safe side in case there (still?) /is/ a reason after all not to
allow that combination in general, lets keep the default of implicit
--with-system-cairo if any of --enable-gtk3 or --enable-gtk3-kde5 is
(implicitly) set.
new_message_clean:
Allow to opt in for --enable-gtk3 plus --without-system-cairo

This check had been introduced with 5ad60c5d69042a73d7a1632d3c04e15783817db4
"more configure, and scp2 pieces for gtk3 integration", but without stating any
reason. In a comment at <https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/c/core/+/104549/1#
message-4b5fcbdabf9c7e40782df682d68efb6282b37c6e> "Allow to opt in for
--enable-gtk3 plus --without-system-cairo", mmeeks now states: "My recollection
is of horrors with the internal cairo being linked before the system one, and
being older - such that various gtk3 themes / bits of functionality which would
now link to an older (or even newer ;-) internal cairo randomly stop working /
crash / burn / etc."

However, at least my Linux build appears to work fine with (among others)

--enable-gtk3
--enable-gtk3-kde5
--without-system-cairo

And that combination proved useful to me when I wanted to run
SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN=gtk3 LO against a libcairo built with ASan the other day.

So, while keeping the default of implicit --with-system-cairo if any of
--enable-gtk3 or --enable-gtk3-kde5 is (implicitly) set, lets allow to
nevertheless explicitly opt in to that combination---with a prominent warning.

[WIP] Handle collisions from SerialProvider::acquireIndex

Why:
* When using the TempUserCreator::create or ::acquireAndStashName to
get temporary account when the chosen username already existed, the
code would cause errors and then incorrectly log the client into
an existing temporary account
* This is very bad behaviour, though shouldn't happen in most cases.
This becomes an issue if the serialMapping configuration is changed
such that a collision is possible.
* As such, the code using the SerialProvider should be aware that
it may produce an already existing temporary account username and
get a new one in this case.

What:
* Update TempUserCreator::acquireName to check to see if the usename
it generates already exists. If it does, then the code generates
a new username up to 4 more times. If the 5 attempts fail, then the
method returns null. Otherwise, the username that isn't in use is
returned.
* Create the private method TempUserCreator::attemptAutoCreate that
attempts an autocreate for a temporary account name, and optionally
logs the account in. This is done by splitting code out of
TempUserCreator::create.
* Update TempUserCreator::create to use ::attemptAutoCreate to
first to check if the account can be created and then again once
the account is created to actually login to that temporary account.
This is done because attempting to login on the first call when the
account already existed would allow another user access to the
temporary account. The second call is required as there is no other
way to login to a temporary account (even though the code knows that
the tempoarary account must exist).
* Update TempUserCreator::acquireAndStashName to respond to the changes
to ::acquireName, such that it returns null if ::acquireName returns
null and also does not modify the session.
* Update EditPage::maybeActivateTempUserCreate to return a Status and
return a good status in all cases except when a temporary account
name could not be acquired.
* Update ApiEditPage to die with an error if the call to EditPage::
maybeActivateTempUserCreate returns with a Status object that has
::isOK return false.
* Update ApiAcquireTempUserName to die with an error if a temporary
account username could not be acquired.
* Add an associated API error key and non-API error key related to
not being able to acquire a temporary account name.
* Provide tests for the untested ApiAcquireTempUserName.php file
including testing the new behaviour.
* Add and update tests for TempUserCreator.php

Lazy-load, use OOUI dialog in video.js playback mode

Retools the video.js player mode to defer loading of video.js libraries,
and instead wrap the native players with loader links that will pop up
an OOUI dialog to run the video.js player in.

This returns us to similar behavior to use of the old popup players but
with cleaner base HTML that works when no JS is available, and keeps the
JS and CSS payloads relatively light on load when no player is used.

Audio players currently use the native default controls instead of
video.js transformations, to avoid adding a popup there. This may change.

The dialog can be expanded in future with share/embed, download, etc
workflows.

Current bugs:
* several missing localizations
* scrolling bit in IE and Edge

Todo:
* fix IE and Edge
* test behavior in legacy browsers that won't play
* cleanup and localization

Future:
* handle audio better
* add share/embed and info in the dialog?

vcl: fix Win32 deadlocks from SolarMutexReleaser

To create and destroy thread-affine Win32 Windows and DCs, non-main
threads SendMessage() special messages like SAL_MSG_CREATEFRAME.

The main thread must handle these messages and return the result to
un-block the other thread.

This works fine as long as the main thread is in its message loop anyway
and blocked on GetMessage(); however if the main blocks trying to acquire
the SolarMutex that is held by the sending thread, deadlock results.

In order to work around this, there is some peculiar code in
ImplSalYieldMutexAcquireWithWait() to avoid blocking the main thread on
mpSalYieldMutex but instead block in GetMessage().

The crucial detail is that GetMessage() will immediately dispatch any
message sent via SendMessage(), which avoids the deadlock.

https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ms644936.aspx
https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/ms644927.aspx

Most of the Win32 WndProc that acquire SolarMutex do so via
ImplSalYieldMutexAcquireWithWait(), but the main thread may also
temporarily drop SolarMutex and re-aquire it with the questionable
SolarMutexReleaser hack, which calls ImplSalAcquireYieldMutex()
instead, which blocks on mpSalYieldMutex.

Fix SolarMutexReleaser to call a new function
Application::ReAcquireSolarMutex() that does the right thing here:
acquire SolarMutex via ImplSalYieldMutexAcquireWithWait().

It turns out that this problem was already fixed before in commit
6a8fd4c76a969ac98d1aff91ff7442f43aee0006 but the problem was
insufficiently documented in the commit and it introduced the bug
that Application::Reschedule() was called without having the SolarMutex
locked, which caused timers to run without SolarMutex, so the commit
was reverted in 1ef1781390845d03b6e1518bbac81b818be62f3d.

page save, in order to avoid exposing the user's IP address.

* Add $wgAutoCreateTempUser, for configuring the system
* Add TempUserConfig service, which interprets the config.
* Add TempUserCreator service, which creates users during page save as
requested by EditPage. With proxy methods to TempUserConfig for
convenience.
* Add new anon warning messages to EditPage.
* Add new temp user warning to Special:CreateAccount.
* Add table user_autocreate_serial. Table creation is necessary before
the feature is enabled but is not necessary before deployment of this
commit.
* Use a placeholder user with a special name during the save process but
before serial acquisition. This placeholder user has the privileges of
a temporary user but is not in the database.
* In PermissionManager, automatically elevate permissions from anon to
temp if the action is enabled for autocreate and the rigor is "quick".
This helps reduce the complexity of the skin changes.
* In AuthManager, introduce a new autocreate source for temp users. Send
permanent login cookies when this source is used.
* On login, suppress the form default for the username if it is a
temporary user. I did it in all three places where the default is
set.
* Treat temp users as anons for the following purposes: login form
redirect bypass, join link; preferences, watchlist and auth change
special pages; create account "proxy" mode.
* Add a new warning message when logout is expected to permanently
discard an account.
* In the skin header, with auto-creation enabled but edit denied for
anons, show "not logged in", but suppress anon talk/contributions.

tdf#141550 tdf#141557 tdf#140975 sw: fix textbox crash

and regressions by refactoring SwTextBoxHelper.

tdf#141550 was a DOCX import regression from
commit ff321dd36554d25f0817903becf4598065e0a194
(tdf#140828 sw textbox: fix AS_CHAR regression),
resulting bad horizontal position of the frame of
the textbox.

tdf#141557 was a regression resulting crash
by changing text box anchoring "To Paragraph".

tdf#140975 was an implementation error, resulting
broken textbox by changing box anchoring to
"As Character".

In the SwTextBoxHelper class there were many
repeating code parts for textbox positioning.
Now these parts have been replaced with
the calls of several new functions:

1) getShapeFormat() returns with the SwFrameFormat
of the UNO XShape;

2) setWrapThrough() only sets the surround
of the textframe (used in the code frequently);

3) changeAnchor() sets the anchor of the textframe
according to the anchor of the shape;

4) doTextFramePositioning() sets the position of the
textbox according to the shape (used in the code
frequently);

5) isAnchorTypeDifferent() shows difference of the
anchor types of the shape and the textframe. Also it
handles the situation of anchoring "As Character";

6) isTextBoxHasValidTextFrame() checks if the shape
is a part of a textbox or not.

Every function returns with true on success, otherwise
gives information to the log. All of them can be called
with ShapeFormat or UNO XShape.

The goal of this to make the possibility to advance this
class for further functions – rotation, grouped
textboxes etc. – without code copying.

new_message_clean:
Fix use-after-free in SwLayAction::IsShortCut

...as seen with valgrind during CppunitTest_sw_odfexport (see below).

It looks like the

if ( !IsEmptyPage() ) //#59184# unnecessary for empty pages

optimization in SwPageFrame::DestroyImpl (which was there ever since at least
84a3db80b4fd66c6854b3135b5f69b61fd828e62 "initial import") was wrong, preventing
the call to

pImp->GetLayAction().SetAgain();

that would cause SwLayAction::IsShortCut (sw/source/core/layout/layact.cxx) to
quit early from an IsAgain() call, before accessing prPage again that has
meanwhile been destroyed from within its

pContent->Calc(pRenderContext);

call.

The same failure started to show in ASan+UBSan builds only now after
integration of <https://gerrit.libreoffice.org/#/c/58263/> "the custom SAL
allocator is no longer used", for reasons I explained in a comment there: "For
FORCE_SYSALLOC (which was esp. set for ASan/UBSan builds), alloc_mode was always
left at AllocMode::UNSET (as determine_alloc_mode was never called in
FORCE_SYSALLOC blocks), so rtl_cache_alloc (which only checked alloc_mode for
AllocMode::SYSTEM, but never called determine_alloc, and wasn't entirely short-
circuited under FORCE_SYSALLOC) actually called into the legacy, supposed-dead
slab allocator code. That's apparently how some use-after-free bug in sw got
hidden from ASan+UBSan builds in the past, and only now starts to show up
(<https://ci.libreoffice.org/job/lo_ubsan/989/>)."

new_message_clean:
mediawiki::mcrouter_wancache: add a failover route to a secondary pool

We've had several cases where the unavailability of one memcached
server caused a severe impact on the latency and availability of
MediaWiki.

This patch introduces (for now, only on mwdebug1001) a
failover pool (the so-called "gutter pool") that will be used by
mcrouter whenever one server in the main pool becomes unavailable.

We chose to set an expiry time to the keys in the failover pool of 600
seconds, which should be enough to guarantee availability in an
emergency, and not enough to cause long-lasting consistency troubles.

new_message_clean:
Only set up DOM aliases once

For WMF CI, we use a hack where we override the version of the library
loaded from vendor/wikimedia/parsoid with the code loaded from the
extension directory check out. That ensures CI runs against the
latest Parsoid code, not just the "released" parsoid code in
mediawiki-vendor.

We used a hack in RegistrationHookHandler to ensure that the DOM
aliases are set up if we're running the code from the extension
directory, even if the version in vendor/wikimedia/parsoid doesn't
know about the DOM aliases yet. But this breaks when we actually
release a version to vendor/wikimedia/parsoid that sets up the
DOM aliases; now we try to do it twice, and fail.

This is compounded by the fact that previously $wgParsoidUseDodo
*looked* like a global, but it wasn't declared with `global` so it
wasn't actually a global. So any test that looked to see if
$wgParsoidUseDodo was set would fail.

So: make $wgParsoidUseDodo *actually* a global, and tweak the
code in RegistrationHookHandler to only set up the DOM aliases
if they're not already set up. There are still some gotchas
here since we're always going to execute
`vendor/wikimedia/parsoid/DomImpl.php`, never the one loaded
from the extension directory, but with a little bit of care
this can probably be finessed. The $wgParsoidDomImplVersion
global has been set to try to make this a little easier.

Fix window sizing and content scaling on macOS when using Qt

macOS Retina displays use a 2 tier system of logical pixels for
windows and views. But they are backed by image buffers that are
2x2 physical pixels for each logical pixel. In contrast, Qt6 on
macOS uses logical pixels that scale like Linux and Windows so
different code for window sizing and content scaling is needed
when the Qt6 plugin is used on macOS.

When using the Qt toolkit on macOS, always assume that the window
will be displayed on a Retina display as an overwhelming majority
of Macs have at least one Retina display. This not only ensures
that LibreOffice windows and widgets are drawn with the same
sizes on a Retina display with Qt as with the macOS native code
plugin, but also ensures that if a window is displayed on a
non-Retina display, all of the QImages related to a window
store pixels at Retina resolution so if a window is moved to a
Retina display, no recreating, rescaling, or redrawing of QImages
is needed.

In addition to providing the usual CSS-only usage examples on the relevant
docs page, this commit also makes some changes to how Accordion.vue
handles the <details> indicator icon.

Previously this was handled using a <cdx-icon> component. CSS-only usage
of Accordion at this point would have required the user to bring along
their own CSS-only Icon element and ensure that it is styled correctly.

This seemed less than ideal, especially since the indicator icon is always
the same; it's not like a button icon where the user may or may not want
an icon and they need to control which one they use.

Instead, the Accordion component styles have been re-worked to basically
embed a CSS-only indicator icon in the *Vue* version of the component, so
that it is also available to CSS-only users.

tdf#147285 qt: Let Qt handle encoding for non-UTF16 "text/plain"

If there were no data for MIME type "text/plain;charset=utf-16"
in the clipboard, but "text/plain" is provided, it was previously
assumed that this would be encoded in the locale's encoding, and
corresponding conversion happened to provide
"text/plain;charset=utf-16" ourselves.

"text/plain;charset=utf-8" data was simply ignored, but using
it (if present) and preferring it over "text/plain"
is more reliable (and e.g. avoids incorrect paste of Chinese
characters from Firefox into Impress when using the qt5/qt6/kf5
VCL plugin on Wayland).

Instead of adding our own handling for "text/plain;charset=utf-8"
and making any assumptions for the encoding of "text/plain"
data, let Qt handle this and just call `QMimeData::text()`
in `QtTransferable::getTransferData`.

Since qtbase commit 589a01ff6b1eacf81e74a5fc4801572135214f43
("QMimeData: Prefer UTF-8 when multiple charsets are available",
contained in Qt >= 5.13), that one handles MIME type
"text/plain;charset=utf-8" in addition to "text/plain;charset".

Rename the "m_bConvertFromLocale" member to better fit
the new meaning.

[1] https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtbase.git/commit/?id=589a01ff6b1eacf81e74a5fc4801572135214f43

old_message_clean:
Add throttle feature to fetchers that may require it

Add throttle feature to {{#get_web_data:}}, {{#get_soap_data:}}
and {{#get_program_data:}} and the corresponding Lua functions.

If a service has been called too recently, the call fails producing
an error message (unless stale cache can be served, in which case
there will be a timestamp in the external variable __throttled_till),
and a job is created that purges the page, when the service frees
(with some limitations).

For {{#get_web_data:}} and {{#get_soap_data:}} throttling
is configured by two new variables:
* $edgThrottleKey (default is [ "*" => "$2nd_lvl_domain$" ])
is an array of throttle key templates. Its keys can be:
* hosts (i.e., domains),
* second-level domains (e.g., livejournal.com for
alex-mashin.livejournal.com),
* '*' or 0 for universal fallback key.
* $edgThrottleInterval (default is [ '*' => 0 ] meaning
no throttling) is an array of intervals between to calls
to the same service in seconds, indexed by resolved throttle
keys.

For any URL, $edgThrottleKey will be looked up for the complete
host, then for its second-level domain, then for the universal
fallback value. In the found template, wildcards like $host$
or $2nd_lvl_domain$ will be substituted by the corresponding
URL components or HTTP options.

The resolved throttle key will be used as index to look
for throttle interval in $edgThrottleInterval.
If it is found and non-zero, throttling will be activated.

For {{#get_program_data:}}, the throttling is configured
by $edgExeThrottleKey and $ExeThrottleInterval, which are
arrays indexed by program ids, by default, empty.
In the found template, wildcards will be substituted with program
arguments and environment variables, although it makes
the most sense simply to set the templates constant, throttling
program calls per program itself and not any finer. Throttling
will only be activated, if both the throttling key and interval
are non-empty and non-zero.

A track of the time, when a service identified by the throttle key
is again available, is kept in ObjectCache::getLocalClusterInstance().
If this time is not yet come, the call to the throttle service
fails leaving the cache the only hope. Also, a job is created
to purge page's caches, so that the page with the error message
will be re-parsed, when it is next called.

Throttling is implemented by the trait EDConnectorThrottled
used by EDConnectorHTTP and EDConnectorExe classes.
It exports two functions:
* setupThrottle() that should be called from class constructors and
* higher-order callThrottled() that should be called from run()
methods.

Page purge job is done by the class EDReparseJob.
It is most useful if the job queue supports delayed jobs (like Redis).

The numerous small edits to other connectors are caused by propagating
a new parameter $title (Title object) to their constructors.

tdf#168002 CairoSDPR breaks SVG text layout

SubpixelPositioning was until now activated when *any* MapMode was set, but
there is another case this is needed: When a TextSimplePortionPrimitive2D
is rendered by a SDPR.
In that case a TextLayouterDevice is used (to isolate all Text-related stuff
that should not be at OutputDevice) combined with a 'empty' OutDev -> no
MapMode.
The DXArray for Primitives (see that TextPrimitive) is defined in the
Unit-Text_Coordinate-System, thus in (0..1) ranges. That allows to
have the DXArray transformation-independent and thus re-usable and
is used since the TextPrimitive was created.
If there is a DXArray missing at the text Primitive (as is the case
with SVG imported ones, but allowed in general) one gets automatically
created during the SalLayout creation for rendering. Unfortunately there
(see GenericSalLayout::LayoutText, usages of GetSubpixelPositioning) the
coordinates get std::round'ed, so all up to that point correctly
calculated metric information in that double-precision dependent coordinate
space gets *shredded*.
To avoid that, SubpixelPositioning has to be activated. It is possible
to hand over that need from TextLayouterDevice::getSalLayout to
detect here, but I think it's plausible that if a temporary DXArray needs
to be created to have it activated anyways, so I think reacting to
having no DXArray up to now should be okay.

old_message_clean:
parser/content-handler: On CSS and JS pages, only parse and pre-save transform CSS/JS comments

Why:

- CSS and JS pages are not wikitext pages. Thus treating them as wikitext introduces a host of problems, including filling wantedpages, transcluding non-existent templates, and adding to non-existent categories (see T307691 for one of the problems caused). At the same time, there are legitimate reasons to sometimes add links or templates to code, but only in comments.

What:

- Added functions to detect JavaScript and CSS comments to the content handlers
- Use lambda expressions to operate on the contents of CSS and JS comments before parsing
- Put pre-save transform into a helper function
- Expose content model to the `parse` and `preSaveTransform` functions
- Define global variable `$wgParseWikitextOnlyFromComments` to control this behavior

SECURITY: Limit subpages displayed on Special:MovePage form

Why:
* Special:MovePage shows the list of subpages for the page
provided before the user submits the form.
* There is currently no limit on the number of subpages shown
and as such loading the move page for a page with tens of
thousands of subpages causes request timeouts when trying
to generate the link HTML for each subpage.
* Special:MovePage does not need to display all the subpages
and can limit the list to wgMaximumMovedPages subpages as
the user who submits the form would only move that many
subpages if they specified to move these subpages.
* A user wanting to find the full list can use Special:Prefix
Index which provides paging.

What:
* Provide a $limit to Title::getSubpages for both calls in
SpecialMovePage::showSubpages. $limit is defined as
$wgMaximumMovedPages plus 1, where the extra subpage is
used to determine if the results were truncated similar to
IndexPager.
* Because i18n modifications in security patches are to be
strongly avoided, hard code the message shown when the
list of subpages is truncated. This should be replaced with
an actual message key when this is publicly uploaded to
Gerrit.

The toggle can be customize-assigned to keyboard, menu, and toolbar,

- notebookbars cannot be infinitely customized by the end user,
so a develop has to add all items. The user can enable or disable.
- toggling dark mode really ought to be done at the OS level,
and typically should be a one-time setting,
therefore not appropriate to waste precious space.

The primary benefit of making it available in the menu
is for QA testers who want to easily switch back and forth.
WARNING: by customizing the notebookbar, you prevent seeing
any future changes made to the program
(until you reset to defaults or blow away the user profile).

It can easily be added to a menu, toolbar or keyboard shortcut
by the end user, so I didn't bother adding it anywhere else.

To avoid completely cluttering up this commit,
I only added Dark mode to the main notebookbar.
Once this commit has been finalized,
the other writer-apps and notebookbars can
also gain this command.

Dev: Caching for intermediary API responses

Adds simple in-memory caching for intermediary MW and REST API responses.
Isolating the service's own processing in this way is especially useful
for benchmarking. This is a strategy that has proven useful in the past,
and is worth committing to the repo rather than leaving in a local branch.

Caching can be activated by setting a CACHE_API_RESPONSES env variable
when starting the service:

CACHE_API_RESPONSES=true npm start

N.B. This will only work as expected when running a single worker, as
separate worker processes do not share memory. If an in-memory cache
shared between processes is required, that could be accomplished with
(for example) Redis.
